correctness.rationale: All real-linear apex functionals on the basepoint-zero Lipschitz space correspond bijectively to signed affine coefficients. Distance functions yield the universal lower bound K>=max_j(1-beta_j w_j)>=1-1/H. Positive inverse-beta cluster weights make every distance expectation equal to D and attain K=D by the triangle inequality. Equality in every cluster-average constraint forces w_j=1/(H beta_j) and then all within-cluster coefficients to be equal, proving global uniqueness of the minimax functional. Continuity gives a continuum of norm-one linear extensions exactly when R>D. An exact rational signed-spanning-tree checker enumerated 172 extreme potentials over eight finite heterogeneous profiles; the infinite claim rests on the analytic inequalities.

value.rationale: A natural k-cluster ultrametric/clustered metric family previously motivates projection studies but has no immediate common orbit center. The theorem gives a closed exact scalar extension constant and unique signed minimax barycentric coefficient vector across arbitrary heterogeneous cardinalities and scales, and a sharp change in dimension of the optimal-extension family at R=D. In particular it quantifies failure of simultaneous norm-one linear extension while individual real Lipschitz functions still extend isometrically. These invariant formulas and sharp optimizer rigidity are substantive, not routine reparametrizations.
